title.raw: 卷四百九十四 列傳第二百五十三 蠻夷二 西南溪峒諸蠻下 梅山峒 誠徽州 南丹州 Volume 494 Biographies 253: Man People 2 - Man People from Xidong in the Southwest 2

sentences.zh: 西南溪峒諸蠻下 梅山峒 誠徽州 南丹州

translations.literal: The Various Man Peoples of the Southwestern Stream-Caves, Lower Section; Meishan Cave; Cheng Huizhou; Nandan Prefecture
translations.idiomatic: The Various Man Peoples of the Southwestern Stream-Caves, Lower Section; Meishan Cave; Cheng Huizhou; Nandan Prefecture

sentences.zh: 西南溪峒諸蠻下

translations.literal: The Various Man Peoples of the Southwestern Stream-Caves, Lower Section
translations.idiomatic: The Various Man Peoples of the Southwestern Stream-Caves, Lower Section

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，臣僚言：“武岡軍溪峒舊嚐集人戶為義保，蓋其風土、習俗、服食、器械悉同徭人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, a court official said: "In the stream-caves of Wugang Army, households were formerly gathered into volunteer militia units called yibao, for their climate, customs, dress, food, and weapons were all the same as those of the Yao people."
translations.idiomatic: In 1133, a court official reported: "In the stream-caves of Wugang Army, households had once been organized into volunteer militia bands known as yibao, because their way of life, customs, diet, dress, and arms were indistinguishable from those of the Yao."

sentences.zh: 故可為疆場捍蔽，雖曰籍之於官，然亦未嚐遠戍。

translations.literal: Therefore they could serve as a defensive screen for the frontier; although they were registered with the government, they were never sent on distant garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: They could thus shield the borderlands; though enrolled on official registers, they were never posted to far-off garrisons.

sentences.zh: 靖康間，調之以勤王，其後湖南盜起，征斂百出，義保無復舊制，困苦不勝，乃舉其世業，客依蠻峒，聽其繇役。

translations.literal: During the Jingkang period they were mobilized to aid the throne; afterward bandits rose in Hunan, levies multiplied in every form, and the yibao system no longer functioned as before. Unable to bear the hardship, they abandoned their hereditary holdings, took refuge with the Man stream-caves as dependents, and submitted to corvée service there.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis they were called up to defend the dynasty; later, as banditry spread through Hunan and exactions multiplied, the old yibao arrangement collapsed. Driven past endurance, families gave up their ancestral estates, sought shelter among the Man stream-caves, and accepted corvée under tribal authority.

sentences.zh: 州縣猶驗舊籍催科，胥隸及門，則挈家遠徙，官失其稅，蠻獠日強。

translations.literal: Yet prefectures and counties still checked the old registers to press for taxes; when clerks and runners came to their doors, whole families moved far away, the government lost their revenue, and the Man and Liao grew stronger day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties still used the old rolls to demand taxes; when runners appeared at the door, families fled with all they had, the state lost the revenue, and the frontier tribes grew stronger by the day.

sentences.zh: 兼武岡所屬三縣，悉為徭人所有，遠戍之實已無，而鄉戶弩手之名尚在，歲取其直，人戶谘怨。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three counties under Wugang were all held by Yao people; the reality of distant garrison service had long ceased, yet the title of village crossbowmen still remained, and each year a fee was collected — to the bitter complaint of the households.
translations.idiomatic: All three counties attached to Wugang had fallen under Yao control; distant service existed in name only, yet the label of village crossbowmen was kept alive and an annual levy collected, provoking widespread grievance.

sentences.zh: 乞擇本路監司詳議以聞。

translations.literal: It is requested that circuit supervisory officials be selected to deliberate in detail and report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that supervisory officials of the circuit be charged to study the matter in detail and report back.

sentences.zh: ”詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved the request.

sentences.zh: 四年，辰州言，歸明保靜、南渭、永順三州彭儒武等久欲奉表入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Chen Prefecture reported that Peng Ruwu and others of the three loosely governed prefectures Guiming, Baojing, Nanwei, and Yongshun had long wished to present a memorial and offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1134, Chen Prefecture reported that Peng Ruwu and others from the three tribute prefectures of Guiming, Baojing, Nanwei, and Yongshun had long sought to submit memorials and pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔以道路未通，俾荊湖北帥司慰諭，免赴闕。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because the roads were not yet open, the commander of Jinghu North Circuit was to console and instruct them and exempt them from coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: Because travel routes were still unsafe, the court ordered the Jinghu North commander to reassure them and excuse them from a journey to the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣人持表及方物赴行在，仍優賜以答之。

translations.literal: They were to send envoys bearing memorials and local products to the mobile court, and generous gifts were to be bestowed in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys might bring memorials and regional gifts to the temporary capital instead, and the court would reward them generously in return.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔荊湖南、北路溪峒頭首土人及主管年滿人合給恩賜，俾各路帥司會計覆實以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered that stream-cave chieftains, native headmen, and officials whose terms had expired in Jinghu South and North circuits were all to receive imperial largesse, and that each circuit commander was to tally and verify the accounts and report.
translations.idiomatic: In September, the court decreed imperial gifts for stream-cave chiefs, native leaders, and outgoing supervisors on the Jinghu South and North circuits, directing each commander to audit the rolls and report.

sentences.zh: 六年，知鼎州張觷言：“鼎、澧、辰、沅、靖州與溪峒接壤，祖宗時嚐置弓弩手，得其死力，比緣多故，遂皆廢闕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zhang Jue, prefect of Ding Prefecture, said: "Ding, Li, Chen, Yuan, and Jing prefectures border the stream-caves; in the time of our forefathers crossbowmen were established and gave their utmost loyalty, but because of many troubles since then the system has fallen into disuse."
translations.idiomatic: In 1136, Zhang Jue, magistrate of Ding Prefecture, wrote: "Ding, Li, Chen, Yuan, and Jing all adjoin the stream-caves. Our ancestors once posted crossbowmen who fought to the death for the realm, but years of turmoil have let the institution lapse entirely."

sentences.zh: 萬一蠻夷生變，將誰與捍禦？

translations.literal: If the Man and Yi should rise in revolt, with whom shall we defend the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: If the tribes should turn hostile, who would hold the line?

sentences.zh: 今雖各出良田，募人以補其額，率皆豪強遣僮奴竄名籍中，乘時射利，無益公家，所宜汰去。

translations.literal: Although fertile fields are now offered to recruit men to fill the quotas, in most cases powerful families send bond servants to insert false names in the registers, seize profit when they can, and bring no benefit to the state — these should be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Though good land is offered to fill the rolls, powerful families usually plant their slaves' names on the lists to turn a private profit, which does the state no good and ought to be purged.

sentences.zh: 則募溪峒司兵得三百人，俾加習練，足為守禦，給田募人開墾，以供軍儲。

translations.literal: Then recruit three hundred stream-cave garrison troops, train them thoroughly so they suffice for defense, grant land and recruit settlers to open new fields, and thereby supply military stores.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, recruit three hundred stream-cave militia, drill them until they can hold the border, allocate land to settlers for cultivation, and use the yield to feed the garrisons.

sentences.zh: ”詔荊湖北路帥司相度以聞。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the Jinghu North circuit commander to assess the plan and report.
translations.idiomatic: " The court directed the Jinghu North commander to study the proposal and report back.

sentences.zh: 帥司言：“營田四州舊置弓弩手九千一百一十人，練習武事，散居邊境，鎮撫蠻夷，平居則事耕作，緩急以備戰守，深為利便。

translations.literal: The circuit commander reported: "In the four garrison-farm prefectures there were formerly 9,110 crossbowmen who practiced military arts, were scattered along the border, pacified the Man and Yi, farmed in peacetime, and stood ready in emergencies for defense — a deeply advantageous arrangement."
translations.idiomatic: The commander replied: "The four farm-garrison prefectures once fielded 9,110 crossbowmen trained for war, posted along the frontier to keep the tribes in check. In quiet times they farmed; in crisis they fought. The system worked remarkably well."

sentences.zh: 靖康初，調發應援河東，全軍陷沒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang period they were mobilized to reinforce Hedong, and the entire force was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang crisis they were sent to reinforce Hedong and the whole corps perished.

sentences.zh: 今辰、沅、澧、靖等州乏兵防守，竊慮蠻夷生變叵測。

translations.literal: Now Chen, Yuan, Li, Jing, and other prefectures lack troops for defense, and I privately fear that a tribal uprising may prove impossible to foresee.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, Yuan, Li, Jing, and the rest are now undefended, and I worry that an unpredictable tribal revolt may follow.

sentences.zh: 若將四州弓弩手減元額，定為三千五百人，辰州置千人，沅州置千五百人，澧州、靖州各置五百人，分處要害，量給土田，訓練以時，耕戰合度，庶可備禦。

translations.literal: If the crossbowmen of the four prefectures were reduced from the original quota and fixed at 3,500 — 1,000 at Chen, 1,500 at Yuan, and 500 each at Li and Jing — posted at strategic points, granted land in due measure, trained on schedule, and balanced between farming and fighting, they might suffice for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Cut the four-prefecture corps to 3,500 men — 1,000 at Chen, 1,500 at Yuan, 500 each at Li and Jing — station them at key points, grant land as needed, drill them regularly, and balance farming with fighting, and the frontier could be held again.

sentences.zh: 以所餘閑田募人耕作，歲收其租，其於邊防財賦，兩得其便，可為經久之計。

translations.literal: With the remaining idle land, recruit cultivators, collect annual rent, and thereby benefit both frontier defense and revenue — a plan that could serve for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: Lease the surplus land to settlers, collect yearly rent, and both defense and frontier finance would gain — a durable policy for the border.

sentences.zh: ”詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The court accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，張觷言：“湖外自靖康以來，盜賊盤踞，鍾相、楊太山、雷德進等相繼叛，澧州所屬尤甚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, Zhang Jue said: "Beyond the lakes, since the Jingkang period bandits have held sway; Zhong Xiang, Yang Taishan, Lei Dejin, and others rebelled in succession, and the districts under Li Prefecture suffered most severely."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1137, Zhang Jue reported: "Since Jingkang, bandits have dominated the country south of the lakes. Zhong Xiang, Yang Taishan, Lei Dejin, and others rose one after another, and the territory under Li Prefecture was hit hardest."

sentences.zh: 獨慈利縣向思勝等五人素號溪峒歸明，誓掌防拓，卒能保境息民，使德進賊黨無所剽掠，思勝後竟殺德進。

translations.literal: Only in Cili County, Xiang Sisheng and four others, long known as stream-cave subjects who had submitted to the dynasty, vowed to take charge of frontier defense; in the end they kept the territory secure and the people at peace, denied Lei Dejin's band any chance to plunder, and Sisheng ultimately killed Dejin himself.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Cili County did Xiang Sisheng and four companions — stream-cave leaders long loyal to the court — pledge to defend the border. They kept the district quiet, denied Lei Dejin's followers any prey, and Sisheng himself eventually killed Dejin.

sentences.zh: 會官軍招撫劉智等，而彭永健、彭永政、彭永全、彭永勝及思勝共獻糧助官軍，招復諸山四十餘柵，宣力效忠功居多，宜加恩賞。

translations.literal: When government forces were winning over Liu Zhi and others, Peng Yongjian, Peng Yongzheng, Peng Yongquan, Peng Yongsheng, and Sisheng together supplied grain to aid the army, recovered more than forty mountain stockades, and rendered loyal service in full measure — they should receive added favor and reward.
translations.idiomatic: While imperial troops were pacifying Liu Zhi and his followers, Peng Yongjian, Peng Yongzheng, Peng Yongquan, Peng Yongsheng, and Sisheng fed the army, won back more than forty mountain forts, and served the dynasty with conspicuous loyalty. They deserve generous rewards.

sentences.zh: ”詔思勝等五人各轉兩資。

translations.literal: " An edict advanced Sisheng and the other four men two ranks each.
translations.idiomatic: " The court promoted Sisheng and his four companions two ranks apiece.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔荊湖、廣南路溪峒頭首土人內有子孫應襲職名差遣，及主管年滿合給恩賜之數，俾帥司取會核實以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered that among stream-cave chieftains and native headmen on the Jinghu and Guangnan circuits, the number of descendants due to inherit offices and appointments, and of officials whose terms had expired and who were due imperial largesse, was to be tallied and verified by the circuit commanders and reported.
translations.idiomatic: In September, the court required Jinghu and Guangnan commanders to verify how many stream-cave chiefs and native leaders had heirs entitled to inherit posts, and how many outgoing supervisors were due imperial gifts, then report the totals.

sentences.zh: 九年，宜章峒民駱科作亂，寇郴、道、連、桂陽諸州縣，詔發大兵往討之，獲駱科。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the stream-cave native Luo Ke of Yizhang rebelled, raided Chen, Dao, Lian, and Guiyang prefectures and counties, and an edict dispatched a large force to suppress him; Luo Ke was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In 1139, Luo Ke of the Yizhang stream-caves rose in revolt and raided Chen, Dao, Lian, and Guiyang. The court sent a major expedition, and Luo Ke was taken.

sentences.zh: 餘黨歐幼四等復叛，據藍山，寇平陽縣，遣江西兵馬都監程師回討平之。

translations.literal: The remnant Ou Yousi and others rebelled again, seized Lanshan, raided Pingyang County, and Cheng Shihui, military superintendent of Jiangxi, was sent to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors led by Ou Yousi rebelled again, held Lanshan, and struck Pingyang County until Cheng Shihui, Jiangxi's military superintendent, crushed them.

sentences.zh: 十年，承信郎琴州溪峒楊進顒等率族屬歸生界五百餘戶、疆土三百餘里，獻累世所造兵器及金爐、酒杯各一，求入覲，詔本路帥司敦遣以行。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Yang Jinyang of the Qin Prefecture stream-caves, holder of the rank Chengxin Lang, led his clansmen to submit more than 500 households and over 300 li of territory within the living frontier, presented weapons made by his forebears for generations together with one gold censer and one wine cup, and sought audience at court; an edict ordered the circuit commander to urge him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: In 1140, Yang Jinyang, a Chengxin Lang from the Qin Prefecture stream-caves, brought more than five hundred households and three hundred li of borderland back to the empire, offered ancestral arms plus a gold censer and wine cup, and asked to attend court. The circuit commander was told to see him safely on his way.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔以施州南砦路夷人向再健襲父思遷充銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼監察御史、武騎尉、知懿州事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict appointed Xiang Zaijian of the Nanzhai Road Yi in Shi Prefecture, succeeding his father Sixian, as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Attendance, acting Director of the Imperial Academy and concurrent Censor, Martial Cavalry Commandant, and Administrator of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1142, Xiang Zaijian of the Nanzhai Road Yi in Shi Prefecture succeeded his father Sixian as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master, acting Director of the Imperial Academy with concurrent censorial rank, Martial Cavalry Commandant, and Administrator of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十四年十月，湖南安撫使劉昉奏，武岡軍徭人有父子相殺者，宜出兵助其父，俾還省地。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year, Liu Fang, Pacification Commissioner of Hunan, memorialized that among the Yao of Wugang Army a father and son had killed each other; troops should be sent to aid the father and recover provincial territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 1144, Hunan's Pacification Commissioner Liu Fang reported a Yao feud in Wugang in which father and son had killed one another. He urged sending troops to support the father and recover land under provincial control.

sentences.zh: 上以問輔臣秦檜，檜曰：“恐輕舉生事。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief minister Qin Hui, who said: "I fear that rash action may provoke trouble."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Chief Councillor Qin Hui, who warned, "A rash move could spark wider trouble."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“恩威不可偏廢，可懷則示之以恩，否則威之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Favor and severity must not be applied one-sidedly; where men can be won, show them favor; where they cannot, show severity."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "Kindness and force must go hand in hand. Win them with grace when you can; use force when you cannot."

sentences.zh: 不侵省地則已，或有所侵，奈何不舉，俾知所畏哉。

translations.literal: If they do not encroach on provincial land, so be it; but if they do encroach, how can we fail to act and let them know what to fear?
translations.idiomatic: If they leave provincial land alone, fine — but if they seize it, how can we stand idle? They must learn what they have to fear.

sentences.zh: ”十二月，成忠郎充武岡軍綏寧縣管界都巡檢兼溪峒首領楊進京，率其族三百人，備黃金、朱砂、方物求入貢，先遣其子孝友陳請。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month, Yang Jinjing, Chengzhong Lang and general border inspector of Suining County in Wugang Army and concurrent stream-cave chieftain, led three hundred of his clan, prepared gold, cinnabar, and local products to seek tribute entry, and first sent his son Xiaoyou to present the request.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Yang Jinjing — a Chengzhong Lang serving as border inspector of Suining in Wugang and as stream-cave chief — led three hundred kinsmen with gold, cinnabar, and regional gifts to petition for tribute status, sending his son Xiaoyou ahead to state the request.

sentences.zh: 詔本路帥司閱舊制以聞，給孝友錢三百貫，俾還聽進止。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the circuit commander to review the old regulations and report, gave Xiaoyou three hundred strings of cash, and sent him back to await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit commander was told to check the old rules and report. Xiaoyou received three hundred strings of cash and was sent home to await further word.

sentences.zh: 十五年，楊進顒復求入貢，以武岡軍不時敦遣為言。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Yang Jinyang again sought to offer tribute, complaining that Wugang Army had not promptly urged him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: In 1145, Yang Jinyang again petitioned for tribute entry, protesting that Wugang officials had not expedited his journey.

sentences.zh: 詔本路帥司閱實應襲人姓名來上，並促進顒入覲。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the circuit commander to verify and submit the names of those due to inherit offices, and to urge Jinyang to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: The court told the commander to verify heirs entitled to inherit posts and to hurry Jinyang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四月，廣南東路提刑黃應南言：“溪峒巡檢、尉、砦官不嚴守備，縱民與徭交通，恐啟邊釁，乞詔有司申嚴法令，俾帥臣、監司常加覺察。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Huang Yingnan, judicial intendant of Guangnan East Circuit, said: "Stream-cave inspectors, assistant magistrates, and stockade officials do not strictly maintain defenses and allow subjects to trade freely with the Yao, which may provoke border trouble. It is requested that the authorities be ordered to enforce the laws strictly and that circuit commanders and supervisors keep constant watch."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Huang Yingnan, Guangnan East's judicial intendant, warned that stream-cave inspectors and stockade officers were neglecting defense and letting settlers trade freely with the Yao, risking border conflict. He asked for stricter enforcement and regular oversight by commanders and supervisors.

sentences.zh: ”宰臣以為沿邊互市，恐不宜禁絕。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers held that frontier mutual trade should probably not be forbidden altogether.
translations.idiomatic: " Ministers argued that frontier trade ought not be banned outright.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“往年禁西夏互市，遂至用兵，可令帥司裁決。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In former years, forbidding trade with Western Xia led to war; let the circuit commanders decide."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When we once banned trade with Western Xia, war followed. Let the commanders judge each case."

sentences.zh: ”前知全州高楫言：“徭人今皆微弱，不敢先侵省地，砦官每縱人深入，略其財物，遂致乘間竊發。

translations.literal: " Gao Ji, former prefect of Quan Prefecture, said: "The Yao are now all weak and dare not invade provincial land first; stockade officials repeatedly allow people to penetrate deep, plunder their goods, and thereby provoke opportunistic raids."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ji, former magistrate of Quan Prefecture, added, "The Yao are weak now and rarely strike first. Stockade officers let settlers push deep into tribal lands and seize property, which provokes retaliatory raids."

sentences.zh: 宜詔與溪峒接壤州郡毋侵徭人，庶使邊民安業，以廣陛下柔遠好生之德。

translations.literal: It is fitting to decree that prefectures and counties bordering the stream-caves must not encroach on the Yao, so that frontier people may live in peace and Your Majesty's virtue of gentle rule over the distant and love of life may be extended.
translations.idiomatic: Order the prefectures along the stream-caves not to harass the Yao, so border people can live in peace and Your Majesty's humane policy toward distant peoples may prevail.

sentences.zh: ”帝從其言，詔守臣一遵成法，務在撫綏。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words and decreed that defending officials were to follow established law in all things and devote themselves to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered local officials to follow existing law and focus on conciliation.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，禽楊正修及其弟正拱，送理寺獄鞫治，斬之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Yang Zhengxiu and his brother Zhenggong were captured, sent to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1154, Yang Zhengxiu and his brother Zhenggong were seized, tried at the Court of Judicial Review, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 初，正修侍其父再興入覲，獻還省民疆土，遂命以官。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhengxiu had accompanied his father Zaixing to court, returned provincial territory and subjects, and was thereupon granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhengxiu had followed his father Zaixing to court, restored land and people to provincial control, and received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 建炎後，與弟正拱率九十團峒徭人出武岡軍，縱火殺掠民財為亂。

translations.literal: After the Jianyan period he and his brother Zhenggong led ninety regiment stream-cave Yao out of Wugang Army, set fires, killed, plundered the people's property, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianyan he and Zhenggong led ninety Yao regiments from the stream-caves out of Wugang, burning, killing, and looting until open revolt broke out.

sentences.zh: 紹興間，潭州帥司嚐招徠之，後復作亂，屢抗官軍，至是伏誅。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing era the Tan Prefecture commander once won them over, but they rebelled again, repeatedly resisted government forces, and at last met execution.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaoxing the Tan commander had once won them back, but they rebelled again, fought imperial troops repeatedly, and were finally put to death.

sentences.zh: 二十八年七月，楊進京等復求入貢，詔以道遠慰諭之，優其賜與。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year, Yang Jinjing and others again sought to offer tribute; an edict consoled them on the grounds of the long distance and granted them generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 1158, Yang Jinjing and others again petitioned for tribute. The court cited the long journey to console them and sent generous gifts instead.

sentences.zh: 隆興初，右正言尹穡言：“湖南州縣多鄰溪峒，省民往往交通徭人，擅自易田，豪猾大姓或詐匿其產徭人，以避科差。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longxing, the Right Remonstrator Yin Ji said: "Many prefectures and counties in Hunan border the stream-caves; provincial subjects often deal with the Yao and exchange land without authorization, and powerful clans sometimes fraudulently register their property under Yao names to evade tax and corvée levies."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longxing, Remonstrator Yin Ji reported that Hunan counties along the stream-caves saw settlers trading with the Yao and swapping land illegally, while powerful families hid estates under Yao names to escape taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 內虧國賦，外滋邊患。

translations.literal: Internally state revenue is lost; externally border troubles grow.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue suffers at home while border troubles grow abroad.

sentences.zh: 宜詔湖南安撫司表正經界，禁民毋質田徭人。

translations.literal: It is fitting to decree that the Hunan Pacification Commission fix the proper boundaries and forbid subjects to mortgage land to the Yao.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan Pacification Commission should fix official boundaries and forbid settlers from pledging land to the Yao.

sentences.zh: 詐匿其產徭人者論如法，仍沒入其田，以賞告奸者。

translations.literal: Those who fraudulently conceal property under Yao names should be punished according to law, their land confiscated, and rewards given to informants.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who hides property under Yao names should be punished by law, the land confiscated, and informants rewarded.

sentences.zh: 田前賣入徭人，俾為別籍，毋遽奪，能還其田者，縣代給錢嚐之。

translations.literal: Land already sold to the Yao should be placed on a separate register without immediate seizure; those who can recover their fields should receive compensation paid by the county.
translations.idiomatic: Land already sold to the Yao should be listed separately without immediate confiscation, and counties should compensate owners who recover their fields.

sentences.zh: ”帝從其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，宜章峒賊李金陷郴州，焚桂陽軍，州將棄城遁，衡州調常寧縣兵救之，弗克。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, the bandit Li Jin of the Yizhang stream-caves seized Chen Prefecture, burned Guiyang Army, the prefectural commander abandoned the city and fled, and Heng Prefecture mobilized troops from Changning County to rescue it but failed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1165, Li Jin of the Yizhang stream-caves took Chen Prefecture and burned Guiyang Army. The commander fled, and troops from Changning sent by Heng Prefecture could not retake the city.

sentences.zh: 世忠峒李昂霄者，率壯丁禦賊，民恃以安。

translations.literal: Li Angxiao of the Shizhong stream-cave led stalwart men to resist the bandits, and the people relied on him for safety.
translations.idiomatic: Li Angxiao of the Shizhong cave led his men against the rebels, and the people found safety in his defense.

sentences.zh: 湖南提舉常平鄭丙請發鄂渚軍討賊，平之。

translations.literal: Zheng Bing, Hunan intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries, requested that troops from Ezhou be sent to suppress the bandits, and they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bing, Hunan's Ever-Normal intendant, asked for Ezhou troops to crush the rebels, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 昂霄以功補承節郎，管轄衡州常寧縣溪峒，及官其子當年，俾後得襲職。

translations.literal: For his merit Angxiao was granted the rank Chengjie Lang and put in charge of the stream-caves of Changning County in Heng Prefecture; his son Dangnian was also given office so that he might later inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: Angxiao was made a Chengjie Lang and placed over Changning's stream-caves in Heng Prefecture; his son Dangnian received office as well, with the right to inherit later.

sentences.zh: 三年，靖州界徭人姚明教等作亂，詔荊、鄂駐紮明椿選將率精銳千人，會屯戍官合擊之，能立功者有厚賞。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Yao Yao Mingjiao and others on the Jing Prefecture border rebelled; an edict ordered Ming Chun, stationed at Jing and E, to choose a general and lead a thousand elite troops to join garrison officers in a combined attack, with rich rewards for those who distinguished themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In 1167, Yao Mingjiao and others on the Jing border rebelled. Ming Chun at Jing and E was told to pick a commander, lead a thousand elite troops, join local garrisons in a joint strike, and reward merit generously.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔平溪峒互市鹽米價，聽民便，毋相抑配，其徭人歲輸身丁米，務平收，無取羨餘及折輸錢，違者論罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict ordered fair prices for salt and grain in stream-cave mutual trade, allowed the people convenience without forced allocation, required that the annual head-tax rice paid by the Yao be collected fairly without surplus levies or conversion fees, and punished violators.
translations.idiomatic: In August, the court fixed fair salt and grain prices in frontier trade, barred forced sales, required honest collection of Yao head-tax rice without surcharges or conversion fees, and promised punishment for abuses.

sentences.zh: 十一月，南郊禮成，詔以緣邊溪峒，州縣失於拊循，致懷反側，或逃竄山谷，其在赦恩以前，並加寬宥，能復業者，罪一切置不問，互市如故，悉聽其便，守臣常加撫問。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, after the suburban sacrifice was completed, an edict stated that along the border stream-caves, because prefectures and counties had failed in consolation and control, some harbored disloyal thoughts or fled into mountain valleys; all offenses before the amnesty were to be broadly pardoned, those who could resume their livelihoods were to have all crimes overlooked, mutual trade was to continue as before with full freedom, and defending officials were to offer frequent reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern-suburb rites in November, the court noted that poor governance along the stream-caves had driven some into rebellion or hiding. All offenses before the amnesty were pardoned; those who returned to their fields would face no prosecution; trade would continue freely; and local officials were to visit and reassure them often.

sentences.zh: 以稱綏遠之意。

translations.literal: This was to accord with the intent of pacifying the distant.
translations.idiomatic: This expressed the court's policy of gentle rule over distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，詔湖南北、四川、二廣州軍應有溪峒處，務先恩信綏懷，毋弛防閑，毋襲科擾，毋貪功而啟釁。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, an edict ordered that wherever stream-caves existed in Hunan North and South, Sichuan, and the two Guang circuits, favor and trust were to come first in pacification, defenses were not to be relaxed, levies were not to be imposed by surprise, and merit-seeking was not to provoke conflict.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1168, the court told officials on every stream-cave frontier in Hunan, Sichuan, and Guangnan to win people through kindness, keep defenses ready, levy taxes openly rather than by surprise, and never provoke trouble for personal glory.

sentences.zh: 委各路帥臣、監司常加覺察。

translations.literal: Circuit commanders and supervisors were charged to keep constant oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commanders and supervisors were to watch compliance closely.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔禁沿邊奸人毋越逸溪峒，誘致蠻獠侵內地，違者論如律，其不能防閑致越逸者亦罪之。

translations.literal: That month, an edict forbade frontier scoundrels to slip into the stream-caves and incite the Man and Liao to raid the interior; violators were to be punished by law, and those who failed to prevent such crossings were also to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, the court banned frontier ruffians from slipping into tribal lands to incite raids on the interior, with legal punishment for offenders and for officials who failed to stop them.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總領周嗣武言邊事，如二年四月之詔，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: Zhou Siwu, overall intendant of Huguang, spoke on border affairs in the spirit of the edict of the fourth month of the second year, and the emperor praised and accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Siwu, Huguang's overall intendant, memorialized on border policy along the lines of the 1166 edict, and the emperor warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 是歲，田彥古死，子忠佐襲職，授銀青光祿大夫、檢校散騎常侍、知溪峒安化州兼監察御史、飛龍騎尉。

translations.literal: That year Tian Yanggu died; his son Zhongzuo inherited the post and was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Palace Attendance, acting Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, Administrator of the stream-cave Anhua Prefecture with concurrent Censor, and Flying Dragon Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tian Yanggu died and his son Zhongzuo succeeded him as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master, acting Regular Attendant, Administrator of stream-cave Anhua with concurrent censorial rank, and Flying Dragon Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 六年，盧陽西據獠楊添朝寇邊，知沅州孫叔傑調兵數千討之，敗績，死者十七八。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yang Tianchao of the Luyang Western Liao raided the border; Sun Shujie, prefect of Yuan, mobilized several thousand troops to attack him, suffered defeat, and seven or eight out of ten were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1170, Yang Tianchao of the Western Liao in Luyang raided the frontier. Yuan Prefecture's Sun Shujie led several thousand men against him, was routed, and lost seven or eight men in ten.

sentences.zh: 初，徭人與省戶交爭，殺二人死，叔傑輒出兵破其十三柵，奪還所侵地，於是徭人相結為亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yao and provincial households had quarreled and two men were killed; Shujie promptly sent troops, destroyed thirteen stockades, and recovered encroached land — whereupon the Yao united in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble began when Yao and settlers quarreled and two men died. Shujie had promptly stormed thirteen stockades and reclaimed seized land, which drove the Yao to unite in revolt.

sentences.zh: 諸司請調常德府城兵三百人，益官兵三千人，合擊討之。

translations.literal: Various offices requested three hundred garrison troops from Changde Prefecture and an additional three thousand regular troops for a combined punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Offices asked for three hundred Changde garrison troops plus three thousand regulars for a joint expedition.

sentences.zh: 宰臣虞允文奏曰：“蠻夷為變，皆守臣貪功所致。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yu Yunwen memorialized: "Tribal uprisings are all caused by defending officials seeking merit."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yu Yunwen wrote, "Tribal revolts are almost always provoked by local officials chasing glory."

sentences.zh: 今徭人仇視守臣，若更去叔傑，量遣官軍，示以兵威，徐與盟誓，自可平定。

translations.literal: Now the Yao bear hatred for the defending official; if Shujie is removed, a measured force is sent to display military might, and oaths are slowly exchanged, the disturbance can be settled of itself.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao now hate the local commander. Remove Shujie, send a modest force to show strength, then negotiate oaths slowly, and the region should quiet down.

sentences.zh: ”帝允其奏，俾葉行代叔傑，開示恩信，諭以禍福，遂招降之，邊境悉平。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved the memorial, had Ye Xing replace Shujie, displayed favor and trust, explained fortune and disaster, and thereby won them to surrender; the entire border was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. Ye Xing replaced Shujie, offered grace and clear warnings of consequences, and won the tribes back to submission until the whole frontier was calm.

sentences.zh: 前知武岡軍趙善穀言：“武岡與湖北、廣西鄰壤，為極邊之地，溪峒七百八十餘所，七峒隸綏寧縣，五溪峒隸臨岡縣。

translations.literal: Zhao Shangu, former commander of Wugang Army, said: "Wugang borders Hubei and Guangxi and is an extreme frontier; there are more than 780 stream-caves — seven caves under Suining County and five stream-caves under Lingang County."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangu, former commander of Wugang, wrote that Wugang adjoined Hubei and Guangxi at the empire's edge, with more than seven hundred eighty stream-caves — seven under Suining County and five under Lingang.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十年，減冗員，改縣為臨口砦。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing redundant posts were cut and the county was changed to Linkou Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1160 redundant posts were cut and the county was downgraded to Linkou Stockade.

sentences.zh: 然五峒之徭俗尤獷悍，釁生毫髮，則操戈相仇，砦官不能為輕重。

translations.literal: Yet the Yao of the five caves are especially fierce; at the slightest provocation they take up weapons against one another, and stockade officials cannot restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the five-cave Yao are especially fierce — the slightest spark sets them fighting with blades, and stockade officers cannot restrain them.

sentences.zh: 況本軍巡防砦柵，惟真良、三門、兵溪、香平有土軍可備守禦，餘有官無兵，其關硤、武陽等砦設巡檢二員，徒費廩祿。

translations.literal: Moreover, of this army's patrol stockades, only Zhenliang, Sanmen, Bingxi, and Xiangping have local troops adequate for defense; the rest have officials but no soldiers. At Guanxia, Wuyang, and other stockades two inspectors are posted, wasting grain salaries to no purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Of Wugang's patrol posts, only Zhenliang, Sanmen, Bingxi, and Xiangping have local militia worth the name; elsewhere there are officers but no troops. Stockades such as Guanxia and Wuyang keep two inspectors each while drawing salaries for nothing.

sentences.zh: 以臣所知，宜復臨口砦為縣，則徭蠻易於製服，汰去冗員，則官廩亦無虛費，實邊郡之利也。”

translations.literal: In my judgment, Linkou Stockade should be restored as a county so that the Yao and Man may be more easily controlled; redundant posts should be eliminated so that official grain is not wasted — a real benefit to the border command.
translations.idiomatic: Restore Linkou Stockade to county status, and the Yao will be easier to govern; cut redundant posts, and the treasury will stop paying empty salaries — a genuine gain for the border.

sentences.zh: 七年，前知辰州章才邵上言：“辰之諸蠻與羈縻保靜、南渭、永順三州接壤，其蠻酋歲貢溪布，利於回賜，頗覺馴伏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Zhang Caishao, former prefect of Chen, memorialized: "The various Man of Chen border the loosely governed prefectures of Baojing, Nanwei, and Yongshun; their chieftains yearly offer stream-cloth tribute, profit from return gifts, and are rather submissive."
translations.idiomatic: In 1171, Zhang Caishao, former prefect of Chen, reported that Chen's tribes adjoin the tribute prefectures of Baojing, Nanwei, and Yongshun, send yearly stream-cloth tribute, value imperial gifts in return, and remain fairly docile.

sentences.zh: 盧溪諸蠻以靖康多故，縣無守禦，犵狑乘隙焚劫。

translations.literal: The Man of Luxi, because of the many troubles of the Jingkang period, found the county without defense, and the Gelao seized the opportunity to burn and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The Luxi tribes, left undefended during the Jingkang turmoil, were raided and burned by Gelao opportunists.

sentences.zh: 後徙縣治於沅陵縣之江口，蠻酋田仕羅、龔誌能等遂雄據其地。

translations.literal: Later the county seat was moved to the river mouth in Yuanling County, and the Man chieftains Tian Shiluo, Gong Zhineng, and others thereupon dominated the former territory.
translations.idiomatic: When the seat was moved to the Yuanling river mouth, chiefs such as Tian Shiluo and Gong Zhineng seized the abandoned district.

sentences.zh: 沅陵之浦口，地平衍膏腴，多水田，頃為徭蠻侵掠，民皆轉徙而田野荒穢。

translations.literal: Pukou in Yuanling is level, fertile, and rich in paddy fields; recently Yao and Man raids have driven the people away and left the fields waste.
translations.idiomatic: Pukou in Yuanling is flat, fertile rice country, but Yao and Man raids have driven settlers away and left the fields derelict.

sentences.zh: 會守倅無遠慮，乃以其田給靖州犵狑楊姓者，俾佃作而課其租，所獲甚微。

translations.literal: The prefect and vice-prefect lacked foresight and gave those fields to the Yang clan Gelao of Jing Prefecture to farm as tenants while taxing the rent — with very little gained.
translations.idiomatic: Short-sighted officials then leased the land to Yang-clan Gelao from Jing Prefecture and taxed the rent, yielding almost nothing.

sentences.zh: 楊氏專其地將二十年，其地當沅、靖二州水陸之衝，一有蠻隙，則為害不細，臣謂宜預為之備。

translations.literal: The Yang have monopolized the land for nearly twenty years; it lies at the land-and-water crossroads of Yuan and Jing prefectures, and if tribal trouble should arise the harm would be no small matter — I hold that preparations should be made in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang have held the land for nearly twenty years at the strategic junction of Yuan and Jing. Any tribal flare-up there could do serious harm, and I urge preventive measures now.

sentences.zh: 靖康前，辰州每歲蒙朝廷賜錢七萬貫，、絹、布共八千一百匹，綿一萬七千兩。

translations.literal: Before Jingkang, Chen Prefecture each year received from the court seventy thousand strings of cash, 8,100 bolts of silk gauze, silk, and cloth combined, and seventeen thousand taels of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jingkang, Chen received seventy thousand strings of cash yearly plus 8,100 bolts of gauze, silk, and cloth and seventeen thousand taels of cotton from the court.

sentences.zh: 是時，本州廂禁軍一千四百餘人，沿邊一十六砦，土兵六百餘人，皆可贍給。

translations.literal: At that time this prefecture had more than 1,400 metropolitan garrison troops, sixteen frontier stockades, and more than 600 local soldiers — all adequately supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Then the prefecture fielded more than 1,400 garrison troops, sixteen frontier stockades, and six hundred local militia — all adequately paid.

sentences.zh: 其後中外多故，今歲賜止得一萬二千緡，而本州財復匱乏，無以充召募之費。

translations.literal: Afterward, with many troubles at home and abroad, this year's grant is only twelve thousand strings, while the prefecture's finances are again depleted and there are no funds for recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Since then, turmoil at home and abroad has cut the annual grant to twelve thousand strings while local coffers are empty and recruitment impossible.

sentences.zh: 禁軍止二百一十餘人，諸砦土兵止一百五人，甚至砦官有全無一兵而徒存虛名者，其於邊防豈可不為深慮？

translations.literal: Garrison troops number only a little more than 210; local soldiers at the stockades only 105; some stockade officials have not a single soldier and exist in name alone — can the frontier defense fail to cause deep concern?
translations.idiomatic: Garrison strength is down to barely 210 men and local militia to 105; some stockade officers have no troops at all. Can the frontier be anything but deeply worrying?

sentences.zh: 若歲增給民錢一萬，俾本州募強壯禁軍或效用二百人，分屯盧溪等處，以防諸蠻，庶使邊患永消，可免異時調遣之費。

translations.literal: If ten thousand strings were added to the yearly grant so that this prefecture could recruit two hundred stalwart garrison troops or service soldiers and post them at Luxi and elsewhere to guard against the various Man, border troubles might be ended forever and the cost of future mobilizations avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Add ten thousand strings yearly so Chen can recruit two hundred strong garrison or service troops and station them at Luxi and similar posts. That could end frontier trouble permanently and spare the cost of future expeditions.

sentences.zh: ”書奏，詔湖北帥臣詳議以聞。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered the Hubei circuit commander to deliberate in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Hubei commander was told to study the proposal and report back.

sentences.zh: 是年，申嚴邊民售田之禁，守令不能奉法者除名，部刺史常加糾察。

translations.literal: That year the prohibition on frontier subjects selling land was strictly enforced; prefects and magistrates who could not uphold the law were removed from office, and regional inspectors were to investigate constantly.
translations.idiomatic: That year the ban on frontier land sales to tribes was tightened: officials who failed to enforce it were dismissed, and regional inspectors were to audit compliance.

sentences.zh: 八年，知貴州陳乂上疏言：“臣前知靖州時，居蠻夷腹心，民不服役，田不輸賦，其地似若可棄。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Chen Yi, prefect of Gui Prefecture, memorialized: "When I was formerly prefect of Jing, we dwelt in the heart of the Man and Yi; the people would not perform corvée and the fields paid no tax — the territory seemed fit to abandon."
translations.idiomatic: In 1172, Chen Yi of Gui Prefecture wrote that when he had governed Jing he sat deep among tribal peoples whose subjects refused corvée and whose fields paid no tax — land that seemed expendable.

sentences.zh: 然為重湖、二廣保障，實南服之要區也。

translations.literal: Yet it is the bulwark of the great lake region and the two Guang circuits — in truth a vital zone of the southern realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it shields the lake country and both Guang circuits — a vital southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 或控製失宜，或金穀不繼，或兵甲少振，蠻獠則乘時竊發，勤勞王師，朝廷當重守臣之選。

translations.literal: If control is mishandled, or funds and grain fail, or arms and armor are neglected, the Man and Liao seize the moment for stealth raids and weary the imperial armies — the court should place great weight on choosing defending officials.
translations.idiomatic: Poor governance, empty treasuries, or weak armaments invite tribal raids that exhaust imperial troops. The court must choose frontier officials with care.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初戍兵三千人，建炎以來，每於都統司或帥司摘兵二千人，以備屯戍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning there were three thousand garrison troops; since Jianyan, two thousand men have been drawn each year from the overall command or circuit headquarters for frontier duty.
translations.idiomatic: Chongning opened with three thousand garrison troops; since Jianyan, two thousand men have been detached yearly from the overall command or circuit headquarters for duty on the border.

sentences.zh: 其凶悍者，以州郡不能製，遂慢守臣，反通徭蠻以撓編民。

translations.literal: The fierce among them, because prefectures and counties could not restrain them, thereupon treated defending officials with contempt and instead dealt with the Yao and Man to harass registered subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The worst offenders, knowing prefectures could not control them, scorned local officials and colluded with Yao and Man tribes to harass registered settlers.

sentences.zh: 州郡非白主帥不敢治，比得報，已晚矣。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties dared not punish them without informing the commander-in-chief; by the time word came back, it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials would not act without the commander's approval, and by the time orders arrived, the harm was done.

sentences.zh: 故戍兵敢肆其惡，一旦有警，復安能為用？

translations.literal: Thus garrison troops dared to indulge their wickedness; when alarm came, how could they again be of use?
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops therefore ran wild; when crisis struck, how could such men be relied upon?

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜聽守臣節製為便。

translations.literal: I hold that it would be advantageous to let defending officials exercise control over them.
translations.idiomatic: I believe frontier officials should command them directly.

sentences.zh: ”帝嘉其言，復問左右曰：“靖隸湖北，今聞仰給廣西，何也？

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his words and again asked those beside him: "Jing is subordinate to Hubei, yet I hear it now depends on Guangxi for supplies — why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and asked his attendants, "Jing belongs to Hubei, yet I hear it now depends on Guangxi for supplies. Why?"

sentences.zh: ”趙雄對曰：“靖州本溪峒，神宗時創為誠州，元祐間廢，尋復為軍，徽宗朝始改靖州，與桂府為鄰，故令廣西給其金穀之費。

translations.literal: " Zhao Xiong replied: "Jing Prefecture was originally a stream-cave region; in Emperor Shenzong's time it was made Cheng Prefecture, abolished in the Yuanyou era, soon restored as an army, and in Emperor Huizong's reign renamed Jing Prefecture. Because it borders the Gui princely establishment, Guangxi was ordered to supply its funds and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiong explained that Jing had been a stream-cave district, made Cheng Prefecture under Shenzong, abolished in Yuanyou, restored as an army, and renamed Jing under Huizong. Because it adjoined the Gui princely domain, Guangxi had been assigned to fund it.

sentences.zh: 近歲漕司匱乏，乃責辦諸州，以故不能如約。

translations.literal: In recent years the transport office has been depleted and has shifted the burden to the various prefectures, and for this reason deliveries have not kept to schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the transport commission has been broke and pushed costs onto the prefectures, so deliveries have fallen behind.

sentences.zh: 宜復舊制，俾廣西漕臣如期饋運。

translations.literal: The old system should be restored so that the Guangxi transport commissioner delivers supplies on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old arrangement and require Guangxi's transport commissioner to deliver on time.

sentences.zh: 靖州屯戍官兵聽守臣節製，於事為便。

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture's garrison troops should be subject to the defending officials' control — this would be advantageous in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's garrison should answer to local officials — that would work far better.

sentences.zh: ”帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，全州上言：“本州密邇溪峒，邊民本非奸惡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, Quan Prefecture memorialized: "This prefecture lies close to the stream-caves; frontier people are not wicked by nature."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1174, Quan Prefecture reported that it lay close to the stream-caves and that frontier people were not wicked by nature.

sentences.zh: 其始，朝廷禁法非不嚴密，監司、州郡非不奉行，特以平居失於防閑，故馴致其亂。

translations.literal: At the outset, imperial prohibitions were not lax, and supervisors and prefectures did not fail to enforce them; it was only through everyday neglect of precaution that disorder was gradually brought about.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial bans were strict and officials enforced them, but everyday neglect of vigilance gradually invited disorder.

sentences.zh: 又兼溪穀山徑非止一途，如靜江、興安之大通虛，武岡軍之新寧、盆溪及八十里山，永州之東安，皆可以徑達溪峒。

translations.literal: Moreover, mountain paths through stream valleys are not limited to one route — such as Datongxu in Jingjiang and Xing'an, Xining, Penxi, and Bashili Mountain in Wugang Army, and Dong'an in Yong Prefecture — all of which lead directly into the stream-caves.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain paths into the stream-caves are many: Datongxu in Jingjiang and Xing'an, Xining, Penxi, and Bashili Mountain in Wugang, and Dong'an in Yong — all offer direct access.

sentences.zh: 其地綿亙郡邑，非一州得專約束，故遊民惡少之棄本者，商旅之避征稅者，盜賊之亡命者，往往由之以入。

translations.literal: The territory stretches across many prefectures and counties and cannot be controlled by a single prefecture alone; thus vagrants, wicked youths who abandon their proper livelihood, merchants evading taxes, and fugitive bandits often enter by these routes.
translations.idiomatic: The region spans many jurisdictions, so no single prefecture can police it. Vagrants, tax-dodging merchants, and fugitive bandits slip in by these routes.

sentences.zh: 萃為淵藪，交相鼓扇，深為邊患。

translations.literal: They gather into a deep lair, incite one another, and become a serious border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: They gather into a haven, stir one another on, and become a grave border menace.

sentences.zh: 如武岡楊再興、桂陽陳峒相繼為亂，實原於此。

translations.literal: Rebellions such as those of Yang Zaixing in Wugang and Chen Dong in Guiyang arose in succession from this very cause.
translations.idiomatic: Revolts such as Yang Zaixing's in Wugang and Chen Dong's in Guiyang stemmed from exactly this.

sentences.zh: 為今計者，宜徙閑地巡檢兵，及分遣士卒屯諸溪穀山徑間，俾湖南北、廣西帥憲總其役，庶幾事權有歸，號令可行也。

translations.literal: For the present plan, idle patrol troops should be redeployed and detachments of soldiers posted along the various stream-valley mountain paths, with the commanders and fiscal commissioners of Hunan North and South and Guangxi overseeing the work, so that authority may be unified and orders enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Redeploy idle patrol troops and station soldiers along the mountain passes, with Hunan and Guangxi commanders coordinating the effort so authority and orders can be unified.

sentences.zh: ”儒林郎李大性上言：“比年徭蠻為亂，邊吏慮妨賞格，往往匿不以聞，遂致猖獗，使一方民命寄於徭人之手，誠可哀憫。

translations.literal: " Rulin Lang Li Daxing memorialized: "In recent years, when the Yao and Man rebel, frontier officials, fearing harm to their reward quotas, often conceal reports and thereby allow outrage to spread, leaving the lives of a whole region in Yao hands — truly pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: Rulin Lang Li Daxing added that frontier officials, fearing lost promotion credit, often hid reports of Yao and Man unrest until whole districts were at the tribes' mercy — a pitiable state.

sentences.zh: 近如梁牟等寇沅州，劫墟市，殺戮齊民，州縣告急於兩月之後，比調官軍討捕，俘降其賊，而人之被害已酷矣。

translations.literal: Recently, when Liang Mou and others raided Yuan Prefecture, plundered market towns, and slaughtered ordinary people, prefectures and counties reported the emergency only two months later; by the time government troops were mobilized and the bandits captured or surrendered, the people had already suffered terribly.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Mou recently raided Yuan, looted markets, and killed civilians, officials reported the crisis only two months later. Troops eventually captured the bandits, but the people had already suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 宜戒州縣或遇徭人竊發，畫時以聞，違者論罪。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties should be warned that if the Yao rise in stealth raids they must report at once; violators are to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties should report any Yao raid immediately, on pain of punishment.

sentences.zh: 仍命監司、帥臣常加覺察，庶幾先事備禦，俾徭人亦知畏懼，不敢侵軼，以傷吾民也。”

translations.literal: Supervisors and circuit commanders should also be ordered to keep constant watch, so that preparations may be made beforehand, the Yao may know fear and dare not encroach, and our people may not be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors and commanders should watch closely so threats can be met early and the Yao learn to fear encroaching on our people.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔給事中、中書舍人、戶部長貳同敕令所議，禁民毋質徭人田，以奪其業，俾能自養，以息邊釁。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict ordered the Supervising Secretary, Secretariat Drafter, and senior deputies of the Ministry of Revenue together with the Statutes Office to deliberate on forbidding subjects to mortgage Yao land, seize their livelihoods, and thereby enable them to support themselves and end border conflict.
translations.idiomatic: In 1175, the court ordered senior officials and the Statutes Office to ban settlers from mortgaging Yao land, so the tribes could keep their livelihoods and border strife might cease.

sentences.zh: 從知沅州王鎮之請也。

translations.literal: This followed a request from Wang Zhen, prefect of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a petition from Yuan Prefecture's Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 沅州生界犵狑副峒官吳自由子三人，貨丹砂麻陽縣，巡檢唐人傑誣為盜，執之送獄，自由率峒官楊友祿等謀為亂。

translations.literal: Wu Ziyou, deputy cave official of the Gelao in Yuan Prefecture's outer tribal zone, had three sons who sold cinnabar in Mayang County; Inspector Tang Renjie falsely accused them of banditry, seized them, and sent them to prison; Ziyou then led cave officials Yang Youlu and others to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ziyou, a Gelao deputy cave official in Yuan's tribal zone, had three sons who sold cinnabar in Mayang County. Inspector Tang Renjie falsely charged them with theft and jailed them, whereupon Ziyou and cave officials such as Yang Youlu plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 帥司調神勁軍三百人及沅州民兵屯境上，聲言進討。

translations.literal: The circuit commander mobilized three hundred Shenjin Army troops and Yuan militia to camp on the border, proclaiming an advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The commander mobilized three hundred Shenjin troops and Yuan militia to the border, threatening an expedition.

sentences.zh: 先遣歸明官田思忠往招撫之，以孔目官為質，世祿等既盟，自由取其三子以歸。

translations.literal: First the submitted official Tian Sizhong was sent to win them over, with a clerical officer held as hostage; after Shilu and others had sworn the pact, Ziyou recovered his three sons and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Sizhong, a submitted official, was sent to negotiate, leaving a clerk as hostage. After Youlu and others swore peace, Ziyou reclaimed his sons.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，前知潭州、湖南安撫趙彥勵上言：“湖南九郡皆接溪峒，蠻夷叛服不常，深為邊患。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai, Zhao Yanli, former prefect of Tan and Pacification Commissioner of Hunan, memorialized: "Hunan's nine prefectures all border the stream-caves; the Man and Yi rebel and submit unpredictably and are a deep border affliction."
translations.idiomatic: In 1203, Zhao Yanli, former Tan prefect and Hunan Pacification Commissioner, wrote that all nine Hunan prefectures adjoined the stream-caves, where tribes rebelled and submitted unpredictably — a chronic border problem.

sentences.zh: 製馭之方，豈無其說？

translations.literal: Are there not methods of control and restraint?
translations.idiomatic: Surely there must be a way to control them?

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜擇素有知勇為徭人所信服者，立為酋長，借補小官以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: I hold that men of proven wisdom and courage whom the Yao trust should be chosen, established as chieftains, and given minor provisional offices to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Choose men of proven courage whom the Yao respect, make them chiefs, and grant minor provisional offices to keep order.

sentences.zh: 況其習俗嗜欲悉同徭人，利害情偽莫不習知，故可坐而製服之也。

translations.literal: Moreover, their customs and desires are wholly the same as those of the Yao; they know every advantage, peril, and deception — and can therefore control them while seated.
translations.idiomatic: They share Yao customs and understand tribal interests and deceits intimately, and can govern them without leaving their seats.

sentences.zh: 五年之間能立勞效，即與補正。

translations.literal: If within five years they render meritorious service, they should receive regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who prove themselves within five years should receive permanent office.

sentences.zh: 彼既榮顯其身，取重鄉曲，豈不自愛，盡忠公家哉？

translations.literal: Once they have won honor for themselves and esteem in their villages, would they not cherish themselves and serve the state with full loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Once honored in their communities, would they not value their standing and serve the state loyally?

sentences.zh: 所謂捐虛名而收實利，安邊之上策也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by abandoning empty titles and gaining real benefit — the supreme policy for securing the border.
translations.idiomatic: This is the supreme border policy: trade empty titles for real control.

sentences.zh: ”帝下其議。

translations.literal: " The emperor referred the proposal for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the proposal for review.

sentences.zh: 既而諸司復上言：“往時溪峒設首領、峒主、頭角官及防遏、指揮等使，皆其長也。

translations.literal: Subsequently various offices memorialized again: "Formerly among the stream-caves there were established chieftains, cave lords, horn-head officials, and commissioners for defense and command — all were their leaders."
translations.idiomatic: Offices then added that stream-caves once had chiefs, cave lords, horn-head officers, and defense commissioners — all drawn from tribal leadership.

sentences.zh: 比年往往行賄得之，為害滋甚。

translations.literal: In recent years these posts are often obtained through bribery, and the harm grows ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Lately posts are often bought by bribery, making matters worse.

sentences.zh: 今宜一新蠻夷耳目，如趙彥勵之請，所謂以蠻夷治蠻夷，策之上也。

translations.literal: Now the eyes and ears of the Man and Yi should be renewed, as Zhao Yanli requested — what is called using the tribes to govern the tribes, the highest policy.
translations.idiomatic: Refresh tribal leadership as Zhao Yanli urged — using tribes to govern tribes is the best policy.

sentences.zh: ”帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，郴州黑風峒徭人羅世傳寇邊，飛虎統製邊寧戰沒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading, Luo Shichuan of the Heifeng Cave Yao in Chen Prefecture raided the border; Bian Ning, commander of the Flying Tiger Corps, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In 1208, Luo Shichuan of Chen's Heifeng Cave Yao raided the frontier, and Flying Tiger commander Bian Ning was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖南驚擾，知隆興趙希懌、知潭州史彌堅共招降之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi and Hunan were thrown into alarm; Zhao Xiyin, prefect of Longxing, and Shi Mijian, prefect of Tan, jointly won them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi and Hunan were alarmed until Longxing's Zhao Xiyin and Tan's Shi Mijian jointly pacified them.

sentences.zh: 二年，李元礪、羅孟二寇江西，攻破龍泉縣。

translations.literal: In the second year, Li Yuanli and Luo Menger raided Jiangxi and captured Longquan County.
translations.idiomatic: In 1209, Li Yuanli and Luo Menger raided Jiangxi and took Longquan County.

sentences.zh: 李再興戰敗，死之，江州駐紮都統製趙選亦戰死。

translations.literal: Li Zaixing was defeated and died; Zhao Xuan, overall commander stationed at Jiang Prefecture, also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaixing was defeated and killed, and Jiangzhou commander Zhao Xuan also fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 初，吉州獲賊長七人係獄，土豪黃從龍為賊畫策，賂吉守李絪，得縱還，賊遂無所忌。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ji Prefecture had captured seven bandit chiefs and imprisoned them; the local strongman Huang Conglong plotted for the bandits, bribed Ji Prefecture's Li Yin, and secured their release, whereupon the bandits feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ji had jailed seven bandit chiefs, but local strongman Huang Conglong bribed Prefect Li Yin to release them, and the bandits thereafter lost all restraint.

sentences.zh: 有侯押隊者，領兵戍龍泉境上，元礪復用從龍計，椎牛釃酒以犒官軍。

translations.literal: There was one Hou Yadui who led troops garrisoning the Longquan border; Yuanli again used Conglong's stratagem, slaughtering cattle and pouring wine to feast the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Hou Yadui held Longquan with his troops. Yuanli again used Conglong's trick, feasting the garrison with beef and wine.

sentences.zh: 賊至，官軍皆醉，狼狽散走。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, the government troops were all drunk and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits struck, the drunken troops fled in chaos.

sentences.zh: 寇之初起甚微，賊伺知議論不一，故玩侮官軍。

translations.literal: At first the raid was very small; the bandits observed that official opinion was divided and therefore treated the government army with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The revolt began small; the bandits saw divided official counsel and mocked the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 方江西力戰則求降湖南，湖南戰則求降江西，牽製王師，使不得相應援。

translations.literal: When Jiangxi fought hard they sought surrender in Hunan; when Hunan fought they sought surrender in Jiangxi — tying down the imperial armies so they could not support one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi fought hard they offered to surrender in Hunan; when Hunan fought they offered Jiangxi — pinning imperial forces so they could not coordinate.

sentences.zh: 其後命工部侍郎王居安知豫章，擒獲之，溪峒略平。

translations.literal: Later Wang Ju'an, Vice Minister of Works, was appointed to govern Yuzhang; he captured them, and the stream-caves were largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju'an of the Ministry of Works was then sent to govern Yuzhang, captured the rebels, and largely pacified the stream-caves.

sentences.zh: 五年，臣僚上言：“辰、沅、靖等州舊嚐募民為弓弩手，給地以耕，俾為世業。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, a court official memorialized: "Chen, Yuan, Jing, and other prefectures formerly recruited subjects as crossbowmen, granted them land to farm, and made this a hereditary occupation."
translations.idiomatic: In 1212, a court official urged restoring the old practice in Chen, Yuan, and Jing of recruiting crossbowmen, granting them farmland as a hereditary livelihood.

sentences.zh: 邊陲獲保障之安，州縣無轉輸之費。

translations.literal: The frontier gained secure defense, and prefectures and counties bore no transport costs.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was secure and prefectures bore no transport burden.

sentences.zh: 比年多故，其製浸弛，徭蠻因之為亂，沿邊諸郡悉受其害。

translations.literal: In recent years, with many troubles, the system has gradually lapsed; the Yao and Man have rebelled in consequence, and all border prefectures have suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Years of turmoil have let the system lapse, Yao and Man have rebelled, and every border prefecture has suffered.

sentences.zh: 比申朝廷調兵詔捕，曠日持久，蠻夷習玩，成其猖獗之勢。

translations.literal: When the court is petitioned to mobilize troops for punitive campaigns, months pass; the Man and Yi grow accustomed to contempt and become outrageously powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial expeditions take months, and tribes grow bold until revolt becomes rampant.

sentences.zh: 其如楊晟台、李金、姚明教、羅孟二、李元礪、陳廷佐之徒，皆近事之明驗也。

translations.literal: Cases such as Yang Shengtai, Li Jin, Yao Mingjiao, Luo Menger, Li Yuanli, and Chen Tingzuo are all clear recent proof.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shengtai, Li Jin, Yao Mingjiao, Luo Menger, Li Yuanli, and Chen Tingzuo are recent proof enough.

sentences.zh: 為今計者，宜講舊制，可紓饋餉之勞而得備禦之實，其安邊息民之長策歟。”

translations.literal: For the present plan, the old system should be restored — it can ease the burden of supply transport while securing real defense; is this not the long-term policy for calming the border and the people?
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old system: it eases supply burdens while providing real defense — the best long-term policy for border peace.

sentences.zh: 七年，臣僚復上言：“辰、沅、靖三州之地，多接溪峒，其居內地者謂之省民，熟戶、山徭、峒丁乃居外為捍蔽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, a court official memorialized again: "The territory of Chen, Yuan, and Jing prefectures borders many stream-caves; those dwelling in the interior are called provincial subjects, while registered households, mountain Yao, and cave militia dwell outside as a defensive screen."
translations.idiomatic: In 1214, another official wrote that Chen, Yuan, and Jing adjoined many stream-caves: interior dwellers were provincial subjects, while registered households, mountain Yao, and cave militia formed the outer shield.

sentences.zh: 其初，區處詳密，立法行事，悉有定制。

translations.literal: At the outset, arrangements were meticulous, laws and practice all had fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Originally arrangements were meticulous, with fixed regulations for every practice.

sentences.zh: 峒丁等皆計口給田，多寡闊狹，疆畔井井，擅鬻者有禁，私易者有罰。

translations.literal: Cave militia and others were all allotted land by head count, large or small, wide or narrow, with boundaries clearly marked; unauthorized sale was forbidden and private exchange punished.
translations.idiomatic: Cave militia received land by household with clear boundaries; unauthorized sale was forbidden and private trade punished.

sentences.zh: 一夫歲輸租三鬥，無他繇役，故皆樂為之用。

translations.literal: Each man paid three dou of rent yearly and no other corvée, and therefore all were glad to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Each man paid only three dou of rent a year with no other corvée, so all served willingly.

sentences.zh: 邊陲有警，眾庶雲集，爭負弩矢前驅，出萬死不顧。

translations.literal: When the frontier was alarmed, the multitude gathered like clouds, vying to shoulder crossbows and advance, facing ten thousand deaths without regard.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier was threatened, men flocked to the colors, vying to march with their crossbows and facing death without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 比年防禁日弛，山徭、峒丁得私售田。

translations.literal: In recent years prohibitions have grown lax day by day, and mountain Yao and cave militia have been able to sell land privately.
translations.idiomatic: Lately enforcement has slackened, and mountain Yao and cave militia have sold land privately.

sentences.zh: 田之歸於民者，常賦外復輸稅，公家因資之以為利，故謾不加省。

translations.literal: When land passed to ordinary subjects, beyond regular tax they paid additional levies; the state profited thereby and therefore deliberately failed to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Land sold to settlers brought extra taxes beyond regular dues, which officials profited from and therefore ignored.

sentences.zh: 而山徭、峒丁之常租仍虛掛版籍，責其償益急，往往不能聊生，反寄命徭人，或導其入寇，為害滋甚。

translations.literal: Yet the regular rents of mountain Yao and cave militia still hung falsely on the registers, and collection grew ever harsher; often they could not make a living, entrusted themselves instead to the Yao, or even guided raids — and the harm grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yao and cave militia still owed rents on paper they could not pay, were pressed ever harder, could not survive, threw in with the Yao, and sometimes guided raids — making things far worse.

sentences.zh: 宜敕湖、廣監司檄諸郡，俾循舊制毋廢，庶邊境綏靖而遠人獲安也。”

translations.literal: The supervisors of Huguang should be ordered to instruct all prefectures to follow the old system without abandoning it, so that the border may be pacified and distant peoples find security.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang supervisors should order all prefectures to restore the old system so the border may quiet and distant peoples live in peace.

sentences.zh: 梅山峒

translations.literal: Meishan Cave
translations.idiomatic: Meishan Cave

sentences.zh: 梅山峒蠻，舊不與中國通。

translations.literal: The Man of Meishan Cave formerly had no contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: The Meishan Cave tribes had long had no contact with the Chinese empire.

sentences.zh: 其地東接潭，南接邵，其西則辰，其北則鼎、澧，而梅山居其中。

translations.literal: Their territory bordered Tan on the east and Shao on the south; Chen lay to the west, Ding and Li to the north, with Meishan in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Their land bordered Tan to the east, Shao to the south, Chen to the west, and Ding and Li to the north, with Meishan at the center.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，嚐寇邵之武岡、潭之長沙。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao they raided Wugang in Shao and Changsha in Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In 975 they raided Wugang in Shao and Changsha in Tan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，左甲首領苞漢陽、右甲首領頓漢淩寇掠邊界，朝廷累遣使招諭，不聽，命客省使翟守素調潭州兵討平之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, the left-wing chieftain Bao Hanyang and right-wing chieftain Dun Hanling raided the border; the court repeatedly sent envoys to win them over, but they would not listen, and Guest Reception Commissioner Zhai Shousu was ordered to mobilize Tan Prefecture troops and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 977, chieftains Bao Hanyang and Dun Hanling raided the frontier. Repeated imperial envoys failed to win them over, and Guest Reception Commissioner Zhai Shousu was sent with Tan troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 自是，禁不得與漢民交通，其地不得耕牧。

translations.literal: From then on they were forbidden contact with Han subjects, and their land could not be farmed or grazed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they were barred from contact with Han settlers, and their land could not be farmed or grazed.

sentences.zh: 後有蘇方者居之，數侵奪舒、向二族。

translations.literal: Later one Sufang dwelt there and repeatedly encroached on the Shu and Xiang clans.
translations.idiomatic: Later a man named Sufang settled there and repeatedly seized land from the Shu and Xiang clans.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐末，知益陽縣張頡收捕其桀黠符三等，遂經營開拓。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiayou era, Zhang Jie, magistrate of Yiyang County, arrested the fierce Fu San and others and thereupon undertook plans for opening the region.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jiayou, Yiyang magistrate Zhang Jie arrested the fierce Fu San and others and began planning to open the region.

sentences.zh: 安撫使吳中復以聞，其議中格。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Wu Zhongfu reported it, but the proposal was blocked midway.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Wu Zhongfu reported the plan, but it was blocked.

sentences.zh: 湖南轉運副使範子奇復奏，蠻恃險為邊患，宜臣屬而郡縣之。

translations.literal: Fan Ziqi, deputy transport commissioner of Hunan, memorialized again that the Man relied on rugged terrain to plague the border and should be brought under subjection and organized into prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan's deputy transport commissioner Fan Ziqi urged again that the tribes, using rugged terrain to harass the border, should be brought under county administration.

sentences.zh: 子奇尋召還，又述前議。

translations.literal: Ziqi was soon recalled but again set forth the earlier proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqi was soon recalled to court but repeated his earlier proposal.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，乃詔知潭州潘夙、湖南轉運副使蔡熚、判官喬執中同經製章惇招納之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, Pan Su, prefect of Tan, Cai Bi, deputy transport commissioner of Hunan, Judge Qiao Zhizhong, and the commissioner Zhang Dun were ordered jointly to win the region over.
translations.idiomatic: In 1072, Tan Prefect Pan Su, Hunan deputy transport commissioner Cai Bi, judge Qiao Zhizhong, and commissioner Zhang Dun were ordered to bring the region under imperial control.

sentences.zh: 惇遣執中知全州，將行，而大田三砦蠻犯境。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun sent Qiao Zhizhong to govern Quan Prefecture; as he was about to depart, the Man of the three Datian stockades invaded the border.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun sent Qiao Zhizhong to Quan Prefecture, but as he was about to leave, tribes from the three Datian stockades raided the border.

sentences.zh: 又飛山之蠻近在全州之西，執中至全州，大田諸蠻納款，於是遂檄諭開梅山，蠻徭爭辟道路，以待得其地。

translations.literal: The Man of Feishan also lay just west of Quan Prefecture; when Qiao Zhizhong reached Quan, the Datian tribes submitted, and he thereupon issued proclamations to open Meishan; Man and Yao vied to clear roads in anticipation of receiving the land.
translations.idiomatic: Feishan tribes lay just west of Quan. When Qiao arrived, the Datian tribes submitted. He then proclaimed the opening of Meishan, and tribes competed to clear roads in hope of receiving land.

sentences.zh: 東起寧鄉縣司徒嶺，西抵邵陽白沙砦，北界益陽四里河，南止湘鄉佛子嶺。

translations.literal: It extended east from Situling in Ningxiang County to Baisha Stockade in Shaoyang, bordered Yiyang's Sili River on the north, and ended at Foziling in Xiangxiang to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The new territory ran from Situling in Ningxiang east to Baisha Stockade in Shaoyang, bordered Yiyang's Sili River on the north, and ended at Foziling in Xiangxiang on the south.

sentences.zh: 籍其民，得主、客萬四千八百九戶，萬九千八十九丁。

translations.literal: The population was registered, yielding 14,809 host and client households and 19,089 adult males.
translations.idiomatic: A census registered 14,809 host and client households and 19,089 adult males.

sentences.zh: 田二十六萬四百三十六畝，均定其稅，使歲一輸。

translations.literal: There were 260,436 mu of fields; taxes were assessed evenly and made payable once yearly.
translations.idiomatic: There were 260,436 mu of fields, with taxes assessed evenly and paid once a year.

sentences.zh: 乃築武陽、關硤二城，詔以山地置新化縣，並二城隸邵州。

translations.literal: Wuyang and Guanxia cities were then built; an edict established Xinhua County in the mountain lands, and both cities were placed under Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyang and Guanxia forts were built, Xinhua County was created in the mountains, and both forts were placed under Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自是，鼎、澧可以南至邵。

translations.literal: From then on Ding and Li could reach Shao by traveling south.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Ding and Li could reach Shao overland to the south.

sentences.zh: 誠、徽州

translations.literal: Cheng and Huizhou
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Huizhou

sentences.zh: 誠、徽州，唐溪峒州。

translations.literal: Cheng and Huizhou were Tang stream-cave prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Huizhou were stream-cave prefectures of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 宋初，楊氏居之，號十峒首領，以其族姓散掌州峒。

translations.literal: Early in the Song the Yang clan dwelt there, styled chieftains of the ten caves, and distributed control of the prefectures and caves among their clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song the Yang clan held the region as chieftains of the ten caves, distributing control among their kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，首領楊蘊始來內附。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, the chieftain Yang Yun first came to submit to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In 979, chieftain Yang Yun first submitted to the empire.

sentences.zh: 五年，楊通寶始入貢，命為誠州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yang Tongbao first offered tribute and was appointed Prefect of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 980, Yang Tongbao first paid tribute and was made Prefect of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，其刺史楊政岩復來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, its prefect Yang Zhengyan again offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 991, Prefect Yang Zhengyan again paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，政岩卒，以其子通盈繼知州事。

translations.literal: That year Zhengyan died, and his son Tongying succeeded to administration of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhengyan died and his son Tongying succeeded as prefect.

sentences.zh: 熙寧八年，有楊光富者，率其族姓二十三州峒歸附，詔以光富為右班殿直，昌運五人補三班奉職，晟情等十六人補三司軍將。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xining, Yang Guangfu led twenty-three prefectures and caves of his clan to submit; Guangfu was appointed Right Guard Palace Direct Attendant, five men of Changyun were given Third-Rank Attendant posts, and sixteen men including Shengqing were made military officers of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1075, Yang Guangfu led twenty-three tribal prefectures and caves to submit. Guangfu became a Right Guard Palace Direct Attendant, five Changyun clansmen received Third-Rank posts, and sixteen others including Shengqing became military officers.

sentences.zh: 繼有楊昌銜者，亦願罷進奉，出租賦為漢民，詔補為右班殿直，子弟侄十八人補授有差。

translations.literal: Then Yang Changxian also wished to cease tribute, pay land tax, and become Han subjects; he was appointed Right Guard Palace Direct Attendant, and eighteen sons, younger brothers, and nephews received offices in varying ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yang Changxian also wished to end tribute, pay regular taxes, and become Han subjects. He was made a Right Guard Palace Direct Attendant, and eighteen kinsmen received offices of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 獨光僭頗負固不從命，詔湖南轉運使朱初平羈縻之，未幾亦降，乃與其子日儼請於其側建學舍，求名士教子孫。

translations.literal: Only Guangjian remained stubborn and would not obey; Hunan transport commissioner Zhu Chuping was ordered to keep him under loose rein, and before long he too surrendered; he and his son Riyan then asked to build a school beside their domain and sought a renowned scholar to teach their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guangjian held out until Hunan transport commissioner Zhu Chuping pacified him. He soon surrendered and, with his son Riyan, asked to build a school and hire a scholar to educate their children.

sentences.zh: 詔潭州長史樸成為徽、誠等州教授；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Pu Cheng, senior recorder of Tan Prefecture, instructor for Huizhou, Cheng, and other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Pu Cheng, senior recorder of Tan, was appointed instructor for Huizhou, Cheng, and the other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 光僭皇城使、誠州刺史致仕，官為建宅；

translations.literal: Guangjian, as Imperial City Commissioner and retired Prefect of Cheng, was granted an official residence;
translations.idiomatic: Guangjian, retired as Imperial City Commissioner and Prefect of Cheng, was given an official residence;

sentences.zh: 置飛山一帶道路巡檢。

translations.literal: and a patrol inspector was established for the roads around Feishan.
translations.idiomatic: and a patrol inspector was posted along the Feishan roads.

sentences.zh: 光僭未及拜而卒，遂以贈之，錄其子六人。

translations.literal: Guangjian died before he could assume office, and posthumous honors were granted; his six sons were enrolled in service.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjian died before taking office and was honored posthumously; his six sons were enrolled in service.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，知邵州關杞請於徽、誠州融嶺鎮擇要害地築城砦，以絕邊患。
